Of 34 files rendering a `fixed inset-0 z-` overlay, only 6 declare role="dialog" (KeyboardShortcutsPanel.tsx:64, DiffViewerModal.tsx:285, ats/SemanticMatchModal.tsx:60, ConfidenceScorePanel.tsx:123, SalaryEstimatorPanel.tsx:88, ats/DeepAnalysisPanel.tsx:177). 13 (not 14 — the original list double-counts ExportDropdown.tsx) overlay files contain no Escape handler, of which ~11 are true modals; the other two (ExportDropdown.tsx:200, WatermarkDownloadPopover.tsx:97) are transparent click-catcher backdrops for a dropdown/popover, a conventional pattern where missing Escape is a minor nit. Several of the affected modals do dismiss on backdrop click (e.g. AgeAnalysisPanel.tsx:73, SemanticMatchModal.tsx:54), so the "must click the X" framing applies only to keyboard users, not all users. Worst case remains ats/SemanticMatchModal.tsx:60-62, which asserts aria-modal="true" to assistive tech while providing neither a focus trap nor a keyboard dismissal path. One of the 13 (app/admin/tenant/page.tsx:211) is behind an admin-only route.

confirmed.title: Editor split-pane resize handle is mouse-only — unreachable by keyboard and by touch
confirmed.evidence:
<div
          className="group relative flex w-[5px] shrink-0 cursor-col-resize items-center justify-center"
          onMouseDown={startResize}
        >
confirmed.impact: A plain <div> with only onMouseDown: no tabIndex, no role="separator", no aria-valuenow, no onKeyDown, and no touch/pointer events. The resize listeners are also mousemove/mouseup only (page.tsx:1180-1190). Keyboard users cannot rebalance the panes at all, and touch users cannot either — which matters because the right panel is what squeezes the editor to zero on narrow viewports (see the mobile-layout finding). The 5px hit target is also well under the 24px minimum touch/pointer target.
confirmed.repro: Tab through the editor page — focus never lands on the handle. On a touch device, dragging the handle does nothing.
confirmed.fix: Make it a <div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" tabIndex={0} aria-valuenow={rightWidth}> with Arrow-Left/Right key handling, and switch onMouseDown/mousemove/mouseup to onPointerDown + pointermove/pointerup with setPointerCapture.
confirmed.correction: The split-pane resize handle at frontend/src/app/workspace/[resumeId]/edit/page.tsx:2389-2394 is a non-semantic div wired only to onMouseDown, with mousemove/mouseup window listeners at page.tsx:1180-1199 and no tabIndex, role="separator", aria-valuenow, onKeyDown, or pointer/touch handlers; setRightWidth has exactly one call site, so pane width is adjustable by mouse drag only. This is a low-severity WCAG 2.1.1 gap: keyboard and touch users cannot customize the split. It does NOT deny them the editor — rightWidth defaults to null and the layout falls back to editor flex:3 / right aside flex:2 (minWidth 340), which is usable. It is also unrelated to the narrow-viewport squeeze in the mobile-layout finding; that stems from the aside's minWidth 340 in the default flex layout, not from the resize handle. Fix is small: add role="separator", aria-orientation="vertical", tabIndex={0}, aria-valuenow/min/max, an onKeyDown that steps rightWidth with arrow keys (reusing the existing Math.max(280, Math.min(window.innerWidth - 300, ...)) clamp), onPointerDown instead of onMouseDown plus pointermove/pointerup, and an invisible padded hit area to reach ~24px while keeping the 1px visual line.

confirmed.title: MobileEditor's virtual-keyboard height adjustment is dead code — flex-basis:0 overrides the inline height
confirmed.impact: containerRef points at a `flex-1` (i.e. `flex: 1 1 0%`) item inside a `flex h-full flex-col` parent. In a column flex container the flex-basis of 0% replaces the used main size, so the inline `height` written by the visualViewport listener has no layout effect. The advertised 'Virtual-keyboard-aware height (visualViewport API)' feature in the file header does nothing; when the soft keyboard opens the editor is not resized.
confirmed.repro: On a phone, focus the CodeMirror editor so the virtual keyboard opens — the container height is unchanged despite the resize listener firing.
confirmed.fix: Apply the computed height to the MobileEditor root (`<div className="flex h-full flex-col">`) instead, or drop `flex-1` from the container and let the inline height drive it.
confirmed.correction: The defect is real but cosmetic and narrower than "dead code with broken editor". The listener does run and does write the inline style; it simply has no layout effect. Even had it applied, `vv.height - 44` is wrong arithmetic — it subtracts only the MobileEditor toolbar and ignores the page header/chrome above the editor pane. CodeMirror still scrolls internally and the browser scrolls the caret into view, so mobile typing works; only the bottom of the editor is occluded by the keyboard. Correct fix is to size the h-screen root (or the pane) from visualViewport via a CSS variable, or add `interactive-widget=resizes-content` to the exported viewport in frontend/src/app/layout.tsx, rather than trying to make the inline height on a flex-1 child take effect. Severity low is accurate.

confirmed.title: pdf.js worker is loaded from a protocol-relative third-party CDN at module scope
confirmed.evidence: pdfjs.GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc = `//unpkg.com/pdfjs-dist@${pdfjs.version}/build/pdf.worker.min.js`
confirmed.impact: Every PDF preview executes a script fetched at runtime from unpkg.com with no integrity check and no CSP to constrain it (`rg 'Content-Security-Policy' frontend/src` → no matches; the backend response headers show only x-content-type-options / x-frame-options / referrer-policy). A compromised or hijacked unpkg path gets arbitrary JS execution in the app origin with access to the user's session. It is also a hard availability dependency and it breaks the PWA offline story: the worker is not in public/ (`ls frontend/public` shows only sw.js, workbox, fallback, offline.html, icons, manifest), so PDF preview cannot work offline even though /offline.html and the pdf CacheFirst rule exist. The protocol-relative `//` form additionally inherits `http:` when the page is ever served over plain HTTP.
confirmed.repro: Open a resume with a compiled PDF and watch the network tab: a request goes to https://unpkg.com/pdfjs-dist@<ver>/build/pdf.worker.min.js. Block unpkg.com and the preview fails to render.
confirmed.fix: Copy pdf.worker.min.js into public/ at build time (or import it via `new URL('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.js', import.meta.url)`) and set workerSrc to the local path; add a CSP with an explicit script-src.
confirmed.correction: pdf.js's worker is loaded at module scope from a protocol-relative unpkg URL (frontend/src/components/PDFPreview.tsx:11), on every page that renders a PDF preview (workspace edit/optimize/cover-letter, /try, CompareModal). pdf.js wraps it in a same-origin blob worker via `createCDNWrapper` + `importScripts`, so a compromised unpkg path executes attacker code in a worker that inherits the app origin — able to make credentialed same-origin API calls and read every previewed PDF, though not to touch the DOM or localStorage. It is not unconstrained by CSP for the reason claimed: a CSP does exist at nginx/nginx.conf:58, but it is `default-src 'self' http: https: data: blob: 'unsafe-inline'`, which permits unpkg, so it provides no protection. The `http:` downgrade risk applies only to local dev, since nginx 301-redirects port 80 to https in production. SRI is not applicable to `GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc`; the fix is to copy pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.js into frontend/public (or emit it via webpack) and point workerSrc at the same-origin path, which also removes the third-party availability dependency and closes the offline-PWA gap.
